## What the business does

Drylining Maidstone is a UK drylining contractor serving Maidstone, Kent. The company fixes plasterboard (drywall) to interior walls and ceilings — the modern UK alternative to wet plastering. A "dry liner" is a tradesperson who does this work. Work covers: dot-and-dab plasterboard, metal stud partition walls, suspended ceilings (MF and lay-in grid), fire-rated plasterboard (Type F, 30–60 min), acoustic plasterboard (Part E compliance), thermal-insulated plasterboard (PIR, phenolic, graphite EPS for Part L retrofit), and taping & jointing. Maidstone Victorian terraced housing is a particular specialism: 9-inch solid brick walls typically upgraded with 50–80mm insulated plasterboard.

CSCS-accredited team, £1M public liability insurance, fixed-price quotes within 48 hours across the ME14–ME20, TN12, TN27 postcode area.

## Local context

- Maidstone is the county town of Kent, on the River Medway, midway between London and the Channel ports.
- The M20 and M2 motorways converge near Maidstone, giving rapid access across Kent and into London.
- Property stock: Georgian and Victorian townhouses in the centre, Edwardian semis in the suburbs (Bearsted), 1930s semis (Loose, Allington), post-war council estates (Harrietsham, Staplehurst), and a steady stream of new-build estates on the village edges.
- Conservation Areas: Yalding village core, Loose village, East Farleigh riverside, parts of Bearsted.
- Local authority: Maidstone Borough Council (planning authority for all 12 areas).
- Building Regulations 2010 (England) — relevant Parts: Part B (Fire Safety), Part E (Resistance to Sound), Part F (Ventilation), Part L (Thermal), Part M (Access).
- Standards: BS 8212 (drylining and partitioning workmanship), BS EN 520 (plasterboard manufacture), BS 7671 (IEE Wiring Regs), BS EN ISO 717 (airborne sound insulation), BS 476 (fire).
